en: Buddhavamsa 6.
The Chronicle of Sumana Buddha:
"After Maṅgala, [there was]..."
The Leader named Sumana is peerless in all qualities and supreme among all beings.
Then, in the city of Mekhala, he struck the drum of the Deathless,
joined with the conch of the Dhamma.
Having conquered the defilements and attained supreme enlightenment, he [established] the ninefold teaching of the Victor.
The Teacher built a city,
the most excellent and supreme city of the True Dhamma—
continuous and free from crookedness.
He caused a great street to be built, straight, wide, and expansive—
the supreme and most excellent foundation of mindfulness.
In the fruit, there are the four fruits of asceticism,
the four analytical knowledges,
the six direct knowledges, and the eight meditative attainments.
He spread it out there in the street.
Those who were heedful and free from blemish,
who had arrived through a sense of shame and vigor;
These excellent qualities they take up according to their pleasure; thus,
by this method of practice,
Lifting up the great multitude,
the Teacher first awakened one hundred thousand times ten million beings.
At the time when the Great Hero was instructing the hosts of non-Buddhists,
thousands of millions attained realization.
In the second teaching of the Dhamma:
"When gods and humans are in harmony and of one mind;"
They asked about the question of cessation and the doubt in their minds; even then,
during the teaching of the Dhamma,
While the cessation [of suffering] was being elucidated,
there occurred the third realization for ninety thousand times ten million.
There were three assemblies of the great seer Sumanas,
all of whom were stainless and had destroyed the taints.
For those of peaceful mind and steadfastness,
when the Blessed One, having completed the rains retreat,
proclaims the invitation ceremony (pavāraṇā).
The Tathāgata offered alms to hundreds of thousands of millions;
thereafter, in the assembly,
On the stainless mountain of gold,
there was a second assembly of ninety thousand times ten million.
When Sakka, the king of the gods,
approached to behold the Buddha, [he was accompanied by] eighty thousand times ten million [beings].
This was the third assembly.
At that time,
I was a Naga king of great psychic power.
Named Atula,
a great storehouse of accumulated merit,
I then [departed] from the abode of the nāgas.
Having gone out with my kinsmen,
I attended upon the Victor and his Saṅgha with divine musical instruments for the sake of the nāgas.
I satisfied hundreds of thousands of millions with food and drink;
having given a pair of fine cloths, each one, I—
I went to him for refuge.
That Buddha, the joyful leader of the world, also made a prediction concerning me:
"In immeasurable eons,
this one will become a Buddha.
Having exerted himself in striving,"
"We shall be present before him.
Having heard those words of hers as well,
I further clarified my mind;
I resolved upon higher vows for the fulfillment of the ten perfections.
The city was named Mekhalā,
the kṣatriya was named Sudatta,
and his mother was named Śirimā.
Of the Great Seer Sumanas,
he lived the household life for nine thousand years.
Canda, Sucanda, and Vaṭaṃsa—
these were the three supreme palaces. There were three million six hundred thousand [of them].
Women were beautifully adorned;
there was a woman named Vaṭaṃsikā and a son named Anūpama.
Having seen four omens,
he departed on an elephant mount;
for no fewer than ten months, he remained.
The Conqueror exerted himself in striving.
Being entreated by Brahmā, the joyful Leader of the World, being peaceful, [arose].
The Great Hero turned the wheel in Mekhala,
the supreme city; and Saraṇa,
whose self was cultivated, [did likewise].
They were his chief disciples;
the attendant of the great seer Sumanas was named Udena.
Soṇā and Upasoṇā were his chief female disciples;
he too was a Buddha of immeasurable fame.
At the foot of the Nāga tree you attained awakening;
Varuṇa and Saraṇa were your foremost attendants.
Cālā and Upacālā were his chief attendants; that Buddha was of great stature.
Rising ninety cubits high,
resembling a golden crest-jewel,
he shines like ten thousand suns.
For ninety thousand years,
such a lifespan exists;
remaining for that long, he—
He ferried across many people.
Having ferried across those who were to be ferried,
he awakened those who were to be awakened.
The Fully Awakened One attained final Nibbāna like the moon on the eighth day;
and those bhikkhus whose taints were destroyed likewise passed away.
And that Buddha is peerless;
having displayed his incomparable radiance,
those of great renown have attained final peace.
That incomparable knowledge and those incomparable treasures—
all that has vanished.
Indeed, all conditioned phenomena are empty.
The Buddha Sumana-Yasadhara was extinguished at Aṅgārāma.
Right there his Jina-stupa rose four yojanas high.
Thus ends the fourth chapter on the lineage of the Blessed One Sumanas.
